title: neato splines=polyline: route to a compass port on the node boundary ends 0.1pt off from C's for some node widths
body:
For an edge routed with `splines=polyline` (or `spline`) to a compass port on the head node's boundary (`"10":n`), the port and C produce different polylines for some node widths, even with identical node positions. In C the path from the tail is slightly bent (x drifts from 29.241 to 29.265) and in the port it is perfectly vertical; with other widths the head end point itself differs by 0.1pt in x (C at the node centre, the port 0.1pt right of it, or the reverse). `splines=line` agrees. The node positions agree exactly, so the difference is in routing.

**Reproducer**

```dot
digraph "fuzz 12614" {
layout=neato;
splines="polyline";
mode="hier";
"10" [label="Start"];
"9" -> "10":"n" [xlabel="\T", color="white"];
}
```

```sh
GVBINDIR=<pango-free plugins> dot -Kneato -Tsvg repro.gv   # C Graphviz 16.1.0
graphviz-pure -Kneato -Tsvg repro.gv                             # port
```

**C output vs port**

```diff
--- c
+++ port
@@ -25,5 +25,5 @@
 <title>9->10:n</title>
-<path fill="none" stroke="white" d="M29.24,-71.76C29.25,-63.74 29.26,-54.56 29.26,-47.55"/>
-<polygon fill="white" stroke="white" points="32.76,-47.81 29.27,-37.81 25.76,-47.81 32.76,-47.81"/>
-<text xml:space="preserve" text-anchor="middle" x="25.75" y="-47.06" font-family="Times,serif" font-size="14.00">9</text>
+<path fill="none" stroke="white" d="M29.28,-71.52C29.28,-63.63 29.28,-54.67 29.28,-47.76"/>
+<polygon fill="white" stroke="white" points="32.78,-47.81 29.28,-37.81 25.78,-47.81 32.78,-47.81"/>
+<text xml:space="preserve" text-anchor="middle" x="25.78" y="-47.04" font-family="Times,serif" font-size="14.00">9</text>
 </g>
```

**Root cause**

Narrowed down with `-n` (fixed positions): head `width=0.81` differs, while `width=0.75, 0.8, 0.82, 0.83, 0.85, 0.9, 1.0` agree (at 0.83 C itself ends 0.1pt off-centre and the port agrees). Confirmed with lldb on Homebrew's `dot` (dumping the `router_t` triangle graph at the first `Pshortestpath`). The head port lies on the node boundary, so the edge goes through the GTS router (`makeMultiSpline`, `lib/neatogen/multispline.c`), not `getPath`/`makePolyline`. The two stacked octagon obstacles are mirror images, so the triangle shortest path (`triPath`) from the head can pass either side of the `9`-bottom/`10`-top diagonal at the same length. C and the port build the same triangles, but GTS returns each face's vertices in a different rotation (`gts_triangle_vertices`, fixed by GTS's incremental construction behind `tri`/`mkSurface`, `lib/neatogen/delaunay.c`), and `triCenter` (`multispline.c:391`) sums them in that order. In C both head edges come out at exactly 20.005238055389295, the first inserted (left) one wins and the guiding polygon is the left sleeve. In the port the right head edge is 1 ulp shorter, so it takes the right sleeve, whose last bend is the obstacle's top corner, and `tweakEnd` (`multispline.c:658`) moves the head 0.1pt right. Matching C needs GTS's per-face vertex order (and, for other ties, its pointer-hash face order), which the port's own constrained Delaunay triangulation (`mk_surface` in `crates/graphviz-pure-layout/src/neatogen/multispline.rs`) does not reproduce. Regression test (ignored): `neato_polyline_compass_port_routes_like_c` in `crates/graphviz-pure-cli/tests/cli.rs`.

Minimal fixed-position reproducer (run with `-Kneato -n -Tdot`):

```dot
digraph G { splines="polyline"; "10" [width=0.81, pos="100,18"]; "9" [pos="100,90"]; "9" -> "10":"n"; }
```
C: `pos="e,29.16,36.482 29.126,71.526 ..."`, port: `pos="e,29.26,36.483 29.026,71.859 ..."`.

**Cases**

No fuzz case of its own. This difference appeared while minimising seed 12614. The full seed-12614 input matches C once the record-obstacle fix (neato-router-record-obstacle-height) is applied, but this minimised form still differs with that fix, so it is a separate bug.

title: neato mode=KK model=circuit: C indexes the conductance matrix by AGSEQ (1-based) and crashes
body:
With `mode=KK` and `model=circuit`, C Graphviz 16.1.0 crashes even on a connected triangle. `circuit_model` fills the `nG x nG` conductance matrix with `Gm[i][j]` where `i`, `j` are `AGSEQ` of the edge's endpoints. Node sequence numbers start at 1 (and on a packed component they are root-graph numbers), so the last node writes through `Gm[nG]`, a pointer read past the row-pointer array. C dies with SIGSEGV/SIGBUS, or, when the stray pointer happens to be writable (as in fuzz case 33861, which crashes only in some runs), lays out from a corrupted matrix. The port indexes by the node's layout id (`ND_id`), as every other neato distance model does, and produces a drawing.

**Reproducer**

```dot
graph G {
layout=neato;
mode="KK";
model="circuit";
a -- b;
b -- c;
c -- a;
}
```

```sh
GVBINDIR=<pango-free plugins> dot -Kneato -Tsvg repro.gv   # C Graphviz 16.1.0
graphviz-pure -Kneato -Tsvg repro.gv                             # port
```

**C output vs port**

```diff
C:    exit status 139 (SIGSEGV), no output (every run on the 3-node reproducer;
      2-4 of 10 runs on the fuzz case s33861, the other runs print an SVG)
port: exit status 0, SVG of the triangle
```

**Root cause**

C: `lib/neatogen/circuit.c:44-50` uses `AGSEQ(agtail(e))`/`AGSEQ(aghead(e))` as matrix indices; `AGSEQ` comes from `agnextseq` (`lib/cgraph/graph.c:156-159`, pre-increment, so the first node is 1). `new_array` (`lib/neatogen/stuff.c:39-51`) allocates exactly `nG` row pointers. Called from `kkNeato` (`lib/neatogen/neatoinit.c:1245-1256`). Crash reports for the fuzz case show `EXC_BAD_ACCESS` in `circuit_model < neatoLayout < neato_layout`. (The stress-majorization path, `model=circuit` without `mode=KK`, uses `lib/neatogen/stress.c`'s own `circuit_model` on the vertex array and does not crash.)

Port: `crates/graphviz-pure-layout/src/neatogen/stuff.rs:445-458` (`circuit_model_kk`) indexes by `g.nodes[..].id`, the 0-based node index within the component.

The port should not reproduce a wild write. Recommend wontfix (upstream bug: use `ND_id` as `shortest_path` and `subset_model` do).

**Cases**

1 fuzz case, seeds 33861. Each regenerates byte for byte with `python3 -I scripts/fuzz-gen.py --seed N` (checked for all of them).

Visual diff: {{SITE}}/whats-left/neato-circuit-kk-agseq-index-crash/

title: neato mode=ipsep with a node in two clusters: C underflows ntoplevel and aborts on a SIZE_MAX allocation; the port draws the graph
body:
With `mode=ipsep`, neato builds a cluster map that counts the nodes outside every top-level cluster as `agnnodes(g)` minus one per (cluster, member) pair. A node that belongs to two non-nested clusters is subtracted twice, so the unsigned count wraps to `SIZE_MAX`, and `gv_calloc(SIZE_MAX, 8)` makes C exit with status 1 and no output. The port computes the top-level node list directly (nodes not assigned to any cluster), so it never wraps, and it renders the graph with exit status 0.

**Reproducer**

```dot
graph "G" {
layout=neato;
mode="ipsep";
subgraph "cluster_0" {
"n1" -- "n4";
}
subgraph "cluster_1" {
"n1" [];
}
}
```

```sh
GVBINDIR=<pango-free plugins> dot -Kneato -Tsvg repro.gv   # C Graphviz 16.1.0
graphviz-pure -Kneato -Tsvg repro.gv                             # port
```

**C output vs port**

```diff
C stderr:
-integer overflow when trying to allocate 18446744073709551615 * 8 bytes
-[exit status 1]   (no stdout)
port:
+[exit status 0]   (a complete SVG with both clusters)
```

**Root cause**

C: `lib/neatogen/neatoinit.c:206` starts `cdata.ntoplevel = agnnodes_z(g)`, `neatoinit.c:231` decrements it once per cluster member (duplicates included), `neatoinit.c:236` allocates `gv_calloc(cdata.ntoplevel, sizeof(size_t))`; the overflow check in `gv_calloc` prints the message and exits.

Port: `crates/graphviz-pure-layout/src/neatogen/cola.rs:21-47` (`cluster_map`) builds `toplevel` with a filter over an `assigned` bitmap, so a doubly assigned node is simply not top level.

The port could match C by emitting the same message and exiting 1 when the C count would wrap, but that would mean copying an upstream overflow bug. Recommend wontfix; mention it in the C bugs ledger.

**Cases**

1 fuzz case, seeds 12208. Each regenerates byte for byte with `python3 -I scripts/fuzz-gen.py --seed N` (checked for all of them).

**Files**

Visual diff: {{SITE}}/whats-left/neato-ipsep-node-in-two-clusters-size-max-alloc/

title: fdp (C): cluster layouts depend on heap addresses and vary run to run
neato-family multispline router: ties in the triangle shortest path are broken by GTS's pointer-hash face order
body:
Edges with multi-edges or boundary ports (`splines=true|spline|polyline`) go through `makeMultiSpline`, which runs Dijkstra (`triPath`) over the triangles of a constrained Delaunay triangulation. When two triangle paths have exactly the same cost — typically a symmetric layout where the edge can go above or below a node — the winner depends on the face numbering. C numbers the faces in the order `gts_surface_foreach_face` visits them, which is GTS's `GHashTable` order of face *pointers*; the port numbers them in creation order. The port then mirrors the route (here below the head node instead of above it).

**Reproducer**

```dot
graph "G" {
layout=sfdp;
splines="true";
edge [headport="e"];
"n5" [shape="circle", label="→ arrow"];
{"n5"} -- "n12";
}
```

```sh
GVBINDIR=<pango-free plugins> dot -Ksfdp -Tsvg repro.gv   # C Graphviz 16.1.0
graphviz-pure -Ksfdp -Tsvg repro.gv                              # port
```

**C output vs port**

```diff
--- c.svg
+++ rust.svg
@@ -26 +26 @@
-<path fill="none" stroke="black" d="M85.73,-34.99C137.89,-25.98 228.99,-13.78 306.94,-21.46 317.19,-22.47 321.8,-20.68 329.21,-27.83 334.35,-32.79 334.19,-43.11 334.19,-43.11"/>
+<path fill="none" stroke="black" d="M85.73,-51.44C137.89,-60.45 228.99,-72.65 306.94,-64.97 317.19,-63.96 321.8,-65.75 329.21,-58.6 334.35,-53.64 334.19,-43.31 334.19,-43.31"/>
```

**Root cause**

C, `lib/neatogen/delaunay.c:447-480` (`mkSurface`): face indices come from `gts_surface_foreach_face(s, cntFace, ...)`, i.e. GTS's hash-table iteration over face pointers; `lib/neatogen/multispline.c:1104-1148` (`triPath`) keeps the first-found parent on equal distances (`N_VAL(pq, adjn) < d`).

Port, `crates/graphviz-pure-layout/src/neatogen/multispline.rs:263-335` (`mk_surface`): faces are numbered in creation order (a documented deviation, `docs/porting/neato.md`, "The `makeMultiSpline` router's triangulation numbers faces in creation order, not GTS's pointer-hash order").

Confirmed by experiment: dumping C's face order with a `DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES` shim around `gts_surface_foreach_face` and feeding it to a patched port that renumbers its (identical) triangles in that order makes the port match C byte for byte on all three cases. The order is address-dependent in C: an intermediate minimisation of s33154 gives two different C outputs from run to run, and both are reproduced by the port when given that run's face order.

Why the port does not match: C's result depends on heap addresses of GTS faces, which the port cannot reproduce in general (it would mean modelling GLib's direct-hash bucket order over malloc addresses). The port keeps the deterministic creation order. Suggest closing as wontfix (upstream nondeterminism); revisit only if a cheap model of the hash order turns out to match C for the usual allocation pattern.

**Cases**

3 fuzz case(s): seeds 23516, 33154, 10372. Regenerate a case with `python3 -I scripts/fuzz-gen.py --seed N` (checked byte for byte for seed 23516).

**Files**

`tests/fuzz-open/026-neato-multispline-face-order` (repro.gv, c.svg, rust.svg, cmd.txt, cases.txt)

Visual diff: {{SITE}}/whats-left/neato-multispline-face-order/

title: dot (upstream C): sametail/samehead on a record node can put the merged port outside every field, and C then routes from uninitialised path-end boxes
neato/fdp/sfdp: unseeded start=random (and fdp start=regular) is seeded from the clock in C; the port uses a fixed seed
body:
With `start=random` and no number after it (neato, fdp, sfdp), or fdp with `start=regular` or `start=self`, C seeds its random number generator from the clock, `time(NULL)`. The same input therefore gives a different layout in C every second. The port uses a fixed seed instead (1, the value C uses when no `start` is given), so its output is deterministic. It can match C only by chance, so these cases are not port bugs. Rounds 1 and 2 of the fuzzer generated such inputs before the generator was changed to always seed `start=random` (commit 6b4ca32) and to avoid fdp's `regular`/`self` (commit 5867090).

**Reproducer**

```dot
digraph G {
layout=neato;
start=random;
a -> b;
}
```

```sh
GVBINDIR=<pango-free plugins> dot -Kneato -Tsvg repro.gv   # C Graphviz 16.1.0: changes from one second to the next
graphviz-pure -Kneato -Tsvg repro.gv                              # port: always the same
```

`repro-fdp.gv` shows the fdp `start=regular` variant (`-Kfdp`).

**C output vs port**

Two C runs 1.2 s apart (`c.1.svg`, `c.2.svg`):

```diff
--- c.1.svg	2026-10-19 09:47:57
+++ c.2.svg	2026-10-19 09:47:58
@@ -4,28 +4,28 @@
 <!-- Generated by graphviz version 16.1.0 (20260904.0139)
  -->
 <!-- Title: G Pages: 1 -->
-<svg width="112pt" height="95pt"
- viewBox="0.00 0.00 112.00 95.00" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">
-<g id="graph0" class="graph" transform="scale(1 1) rotate(0) translate(4 91.38)">
+<svg width="122pt" height="84pt"
+ viewBox="0.00 0.00 122.00 84.00" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">
+<g id="graph0" class="graph" transform="scale(1 1) rotate(0) translate(4 79.57)">
 <title>G</title>
-<polygon fill="white" stroke="none" points="-4,4 -4,-91.38 108.44,-91.38 108.44,4 -4,4"/>
+<polygon fill="white" stroke="none" points="-4,4 -4,-79.57 118.15,-79.57 118.15,4 -4,4"/>
 <!-- a -->
 <g id="node1" class="node">
 <title>a</title>
-<ellipse fill="none" stroke="black" cx="27" cy="-69.38" rx="27" ry="18"/>
-<text xml:space="preserve" text-anchor="middle" x="27" y="-65.18" font-family="Times,serif" font-size="14.00">a</text>
+<ellipse fill="none" stroke="black" cx="27" cy="-18" rx="27" ry="18"/>
+<text xml:space="preserve" text-anchor="middle" x="27" y="-13.8" font-family="Times,serif" font-size="14.00">a</text>
 </g>
 <!-- b -->
 <g id="node2" class="node">
 <title>b</title>
-<ellipse fill="none" stroke="black" cx="77.44" cy="-18" rx="27" ry="18"/>
-<text xml:space="preserve" text-anchor="middle" x="77.44" y="-13.8" font-family="Times,serif" font-size="14.00">b</text>
+<ellipse fill="none" stroke="black" cx="87.15" cy="-57.57" rx="27" ry="18"/>
+<text xml:space="preserve" text-anchor="middle" x="87.15" y="-53.37" font-family="Times,serif" font-size="14.00">b</text>
```

With an explicit seed (`start=random1`), C and the port are byte-identical on the reproducer and on all six `start=random` cases below.

**Root cause**

C, `lib/neatogen/neatoinit.c:942-948` (`setSeed`, used by neato, fdp and sfdp): with `INIT_RANDOM` and no digits after `random`, `seed = (unsigned) time(NULL)`. C then writes the seed back with `agset(G, "start", ...)`, which does not reach SVG output. C, `lib/fdpgen/tlayout.c:481-487` (`init_params`): when the mode is not `INIT_RANDOM` (`regular`, `self`), `local_seed = (long)time(NULL)` before `srand48`.

Port, `crates/graphviz-pure-layout/src/neatogen/neatoinit.rs:130-139` (`set_seed`): uses seed 1 when no number follows. `crates/graphviz-pure-layout/src/fdpgen/tlayout.rs:465-471`: uses `DFLT_SEED` instead of the clock. Both are deliberate, so the port stays reproducible.

This is intended behaviour on both sides, not a bug to fix. Close as wontfix. A test against C has to give `start` a seed (`start=randomN` or `start=N`), and fdp tests should not use `start=regular|self`.

**Cases**

11 fuzz cases from rounds 1 and 2: `start=random` with neato (1259, 787), fdp (1213, 1308) and sfdp (821, 584), and fdp `start=regular` (10718, 10601, 938, 11850, 12031). Each `start=random` case was confirmed by replacing the value with `random1`, after which the port matched C. Each `start=regular` case was confirmed by running C three times 1.1 s apart: C gave three different outputs every time. The current generator no longer produces these inputs, so `python3 -I scripts/fuzz-gen.py --seed N` gives a different case for these seeds. Use the archived case files listed in `cases.txt`.

title: sfdp smoothing=rng: C's output changes from run to run (port matches one of C's outputs)
body:
With `smoothing=rng`, C sfdp gives different layouts on repeated runs of the same input (the reproducer gives 2 distinct outputs in 12 runs; the original case 4 in 10). Removing `smoothing=rng` makes C deterministic (16/16 identical). The port is deterministic and its output equals one of C's outputs, so there is nothing to fix in the port; this records the C nondeterminism so the case is not re-triaged.

**Reproducer**

```dot
graph "fuzz 23510" {
layout=sfdp;
smoothing="rng";
{"v28" "v7" "v39"} -- "v11";
"v1" -- subgraph "s83" {"v42" "v33"};
"v44":"c" -- "v42" [tailport="s"];
"v39" -- "v42" [arrowsize="2.45"];
"v27" -- subgraph "s114" {"v45" "v38" "v1"};
"v20" -- "v11" [label="עברית\lπ\ltab	here\ltab	here\n"];
}

GVBINDIR=<pango-free plugins> dot -Ksfdp -Tsvg repro.gv   # C Graphviz 16.1.0
graphviz-pure -Ksfdp -Tsvg repro.gv                              # port
```

**C output vs port**

The port's output (`rust.svg`) is identical to C run A (`c.svg`). Two C runs of the same command differ (first lines of the diff):

**Root cause**

C, `lib/sfdpgen/post_process.c:968-980`: `smoothing=rng` runs `TriangleSmoother_new(A, dim, x, false)`, which builds its graph with `call_tri2` (`lib/neatogen/call_tri.c:64`, `UG_graph` from `lib/neatogen/delaunay.c`, a GTS Delaunay triangulation). The run-to-run dependence is in this path (removing the option removes it); the exact address-dependent step (most likely GTS's pointer-keyed hash iteration, as in neato-multispline-face-order) is root cause not yet confirmed.

Port: `crates/graphviz-pure-layout/src/sfdpgen` is deterministic. Suggest wontfix (upstream nondeterminism); the fuzz harness already classifies this as `c_unstable` when it catches two different C runs.

title: Linux/WASM: portable libm differs from Apple's pow/sin/cos/atan2 (2470/2589 e2e)
body:
On Linux and in the WASM build, the port uses portable math functions (`graphviz_pure_core::math::portable`), because macOS's `libsystem_m`, the libm that C Graphviz uses on macOS and that the goldens were made with, is closed source. Apple's `pow`, `sin`, `cos` and `atan2` give a different last bit from both the musl-derived `libm` crate and correctly rounded implementations on some inputs. One bit is enough to move a force-directed layout. With Apple's libm the port matches C on all 2,589 `gv-diff e2e` outputs. With portable math it matches 2,470: 114 sfdp, 3 fdp, 1 circo and 1 main (`gallery_beautify_1_1cfb90`, an sfdp graph). The same files explain the portable layout ratchets: main 564/565, sfdp 183/297, fdp 382/386, circo 279/280. twopi's one extra portable miss, `wild_gv16_graphs_arrows_148b6b`, is one of the C-unstable arrows graphs. Linux aarch64, Linux x86_64 and wasm32 produce bit-identical output to each other (`docs/porting/libm.md`, "Linux and wasm32").

**Reproducer**

The smallest affected file is `tests/wild/gallery_beautify_1_1cfb90.gv` (the main corpus's only portable miss):

```dot
digraph G {
    layout="sfdp"
    beautify=false

    N0 -> {N1; N2; N3; N4; N5; N6}
}
```

```sh
GVBINDIR=<pango-free plugins> dot -Tsvg repro.gv                      # macOS C, Apple libm
cargo build --release -p graphviz-pure-cli --features graphviz-pure-core/portable-math     # or any Linux / WASM build
graphviz-pure -Tsvg repro.gv
```

**C output vs port**

The outputs are not attached here. The affected files and baselines are listed in `corpus.txt`: `tests/golden/e2e-baseline.json` vs `tests/golden/e2e-baseline.portable.json`, and `tests/golden/<engine>-baseline.json` vs `<engine>-baseline.portable.json`.

**Root cause**

All transcendental calls go through `crates/graphviz-pure-core/src/math/mod.rs` (`PORTABLE` at line 25). There, `powf` (line 71) uses a Rust port of CORE-MATH's correctly rounded `pow` (`crates/graphviz-pure-core/src/math/portable/pow/`), `hypot` uses a formula that matches Apple on every tested input, and `atan2` (line 83), `sin` (line 95), `cos` (line 103) and the rest come from the `libm` crate. The C side is not Graphviz code: C calls the platform libm. Measured contributions, swapping one function at a time (`docs/porting/libm.md`, "Which function moves which corpus", measured before the CORE-MATH `pow` port): `pow` sfdp 127, neato 3, main 1; `atan2` fdp 3; `sin` fdp 2; `cos` circo 1, fdp 3. The CORE-MATH `pow` port has since fixed neato and 13 sfdp files. The breakdown for the remaining 119 files has not been measured again per function, so this is one issue rather than one per function.

**Why the port does not match:** matching bit for bit would mean reproducing Apple's closed `pow`/`sin`/`cos`/`atan2` from the binary (the published Libm `Source/ARM/*.s` files are empty). That raises a licensing question and has not been done. Correctly rounded `sin`/`cos` would be worse (circo 274/280), and correctly rounded `atan2` gains nothing. The port is exact on macOS and deterministic across all other platforms. The portable baselines (`*.portable.json`) catch regressions there.

**Cases**

119 e2e outputs. The full list is in `corpus.txt` and `cases.txt` (sfdp 114, fdp 3, circo 1, main 1).

title: twopi: edge routes on the arrows graphs change from run to run in C (floating-point tie)
body:
On the `arrows` family of graphs (`twopi`, `splines=true`), C Graphviz 16.1.0 does not give the same output from one run to the next. Nodes `Z`, `i` and `I` (and their mirror images lower down) are exactly vertically aligned, so the edge between `Z` and `I` has a tie: it can run straight, pass the obstacle in between on the left, or pass it on the right. The same C binary gives 3 or 4 different SVGs over 20 runs of each of the 8 files. The port is deterministic. It always produces one of these routes, but its combination of routes for the whole file matches a C run only some of the time (in 20 runs, `oldarrows` matched 2 of them and the other 7 files matched none). This is why `gv-diff` shows twopi at 282/289 exact and why `gv-diff e2e` records the 8 files as unstable and skips them (`tests/golden/e2e.json`, `unstable`).

**Reproducer**

```dot

  // leave some space for the head/taillabels

  // to avoid confusion, remember this:
  // it's spelt tail/head, but it's read start/end

  // emphasize theatrically
//  edge [arrowsize=2]
  // put head/tail labels farther from the node
  edge [labeldistance=3]

  // not interested in node labels
  node [shape=circle width=0.5 label=""]

  {
    edge [dir=back samehead=ahead]
    a->Z [arrowtail=none taillabel=none]
    b->Z [arrowtail=normal taillabel=normal]
    c->Z [arrowtail=inv taillabel=inv]
    d->Z [arrowtail=dot taillabel=dot]
    e->Z [arrowtail=odot taillabel=odot]
    f->Z [arrowtail=invdot taillabel=invdot]
    g->Z [arrowtail=invodot taillabel=invodot]

    i->Z [arrowtail=halfopen taillabel=halfopen arrowhead=inv headlabel=samehead]
    j->Z [arrowtail=empty taillabel=empty]

  {
    edge [dir=forward sametail=atail]

graphviz-pure -Ktwopi -Tsvg repro.gv

**C output vs port** (C's most frequent variant vs the port; `c-variant2.svg` is a second C run, where the same edge is straight)

--- c.svg	2026-10-19 09:18:53
+++ rust.svg	2026-10-19 09:18:53
@@ -128,10 +128,10 @@

-<path fill="none" stroke="black" d="M297.2,-306.09C315.04,-347.89 355.19,-459.08 318.19,-540.71 317.14,-543.02 315.67,-545.11 313.93,-546.99"/>

```

**Root cause**

The routing happens in the neato spline code that twopi uses: `lib/neatogen/neatosplines.c:633-705` (`_spline_edges`: the visibility-graph path from `getPath`/`Pobspath`, then `makeSpline` at `lib/neatogen/neatosplines.c:538`). In the port this is `crates/graphviz-pure-layout/src/neatogen/neatosplines.rs:135` (`spline_edges_route`) and `crates/graphviz-pure-layout/src/neatogen/routing.rs:193` (`make_spline`). The node positions are the same in every C run; only the edge routes change. The C output still varies with `MallocPreScribble=1 MallocScribble=1`, so reads of uninitialised heap memory are unlikely, and the variation probably comes from something that depends on addresses. The exact C statement has **not been confirmed yet**. One candidate is `cmpitems` (`lib/neatogen/neatosplines.c:124`), which orders multi-edge keys by node pointer, but no link from it to the route has been shown. The documentation used to say this tie differs from build to build (`docs/porting/circo-twopi.md:32-37`). In fact the same build differs from run to run.

**Why the port does not match:** no single deterministic output can match an output that changes between runs. The port computes the routes in a fixed order and returns the same SVG every time. We propose closing this as upstream C nondeterminism. If the C source is found and turns out to be deterministic under some condition, the port could follow it.

**Cases**

8 corpus files (all twopi `arrows` variants): `tests/twopi/fx_arrows.gv`, `tests/twopi/wild_gv16_directed_oldarrows_f70da3.gv`, `tests/twopi/wild_gv16_graphs_arrows_148b6b.gv`, `tests/twopi/wild_gv16_graphs_arrowsize_46ccd8.gv`, `tests/twopi/wild_gv16_graphs_newarrows_769825.gv`, `tests/twopi/wild_gv16_linux_x86_arrows_dot_1ce23f.gv`, `tests/twopi/wild_wild_graphs_arrows_a4826e.gv`, `tests/twopi/wild_wild_graphs_arrowsize_ccef6e.gv`.

title: -Tplain: C prints freed memory for Latin-1/entity-converted labels (use-after-free in canon)
body:
With `-Tplain` and `-Tplain-ext`, C prints freed memory in place of a node label when the label text changed during conversion (`latin1ToUTF8` for `charset=latin1`, or `htmlEntityUTF8` for entities such as `∞`) and does not need quoting. The label field then contains whatever the freed allocation holds: on macOS a control byte that differs between runs (`^E`, `^F`, ...). The port prints the converted label (`été`).

**Reproducer** (the file is Latin-1: the label bytes are `E9 74 E9`)

```dot
graph G {
charset=latin1
a [label="\xe9t\xe9"]
}
```

```sh
GVBINDIR=<pango-free plugins> dot -Tplain repro.gv     # two different outputs over 6 runs
graphviz-pure -Tplain repro.gv
```

**C output vs port**

```diff
--- c.plain
+++ rust.plain
@@ -1,3 +1,3 @@
 graph 1 0.75 0.5
-node a 0.375 0.25 0.75 0.5 \x05 solid ellipse black lightgrey
+node a 0.375 0.25 0.75 0.5 été solid ellipse black lightgrey
 stop
```

**Root cause**

`canon` (`lib/common/output.c:103-108`) interns the label with `agstrdup` and passes it to `agstrcanon`, then frees it with `agstrfree`. When the string needs no quotes, `_agstrcanon` returns its argument itself (`lib/cgraph/write.c:202`, `return arg;`) instead of the scratch buffer. If nothing else holds a reference to the interned string (the converted text is new), `agstrfree` releases it and `writenodeandport`/`write_plain` (`lib/common/output.c:153-158`, and line 202 for edge labels) print a dangling pointer. This is a use-after-free in C. The port (`crates/graphviz-pure-render/src/emit/output.rs:219-221`, `canon_str`) prints the converted text, which is what C intends.

**Why the port should not match:** the C output is undefined behaviour and changes between runs. `gv-diff render` skips these references (`crates/graphviz-pure-diff/src/render.rs:21-46`, `UNSTABLE`). This should be reported upstream: `canon` should copy the result before `agstrfree`.

**Cases**

10 render-corpus references per format (`plain` and `plain-ext`): `charset_Latin1`, `charset_b34`, `charset_b56`, `charset_b60`, `charset_latin1_html`, `charset_latin1_mixed`, `gallery__index_7_fe2a40`, `gv16_graphs_Symbol_af1a2d`, `gv16_graphs_b34_ca01c7`, `gv16_graphs_b56_36f937`.

title: -Txdot: C prints its own string constants for HTML cells with STYLE="dashed" (out-of-bounds read in xdot_style)
body:
With `-Txdot` (and the other formats built on the xdot renderer: `-Tdot` output's `_ldraw_` attributes, `-Tjson`), an HTML-like table cell with `STYLE="dashed"` or `STYLE="dotted"` makes C print a run of unrelated string constants from its own binary into the drawing: format strings, file names and assertion texts. The port prints the style the cell asked for (`S 6 -dashed`). **Reproducer** ```dot digraph { n [shape=box label=<
x
>] } ``` ```sh GVBINDIR= dot -Txdot repro.gv graphviz-pure -Txdot repro.gv ``` **C output vs port** (C's line shortened) ```diff -_ldraw_="S 5 -solid c 7 -#000000 p 4 17.5 4 17.5 32.8 36.5 32.8 36.5 4 S 1095 -dashed(dotted,invis,invisible,bold,setlinewidth,filled,unfilled,tapered,gvrender_set_style: unsupported style %s - ignoring\n,gvrender_usershape,gvrender.c,name,name[0],color %s,%s is not a known color. ... +_ldraw_="S 5 -solid c 7 -#000000 p 4 17.5 4 17.5 32.8 36.5 32.8 36.5 4 S 6 -dashed c 7 -#000000 p 4 20.5 7 20.5 29.8 33.5 29.8 33.5 7 F 14 11 -Times-Roman c 7 -#000000 T 23.5 12.8 -1 7 1 -x ", ``` **Root cause** `doBorder` (`lib/common/htmltable.c:261-268`) passes the style as `sptr[0] = "dashed"`, a plain string literal. Style lists elsewhere come from `parse_style`, where each entry is `name\0arg\0arg\0\0`: a name followed by its arguments and an empty string. `xdot_style` (`plugin/core/gvrender_core_dot.c:186-199`) relies on that layout: after the name it skips one NUL and, while the next byte is not NUL, reads arguments. For the literal `"dashed"` the next bytes belong to whatever constants the compiler placed after it, so C reads past the end of the string (undefined behaviour) until it happens to hit two NULs in a row. What it prints depends on the binary's string-table layout. The port builds the same style in `crates/graphviz-pure-render/src/emit/html.rs:181` and prints just the name, which is what C means to do. **Why the port should not match:** the C output is an out-of-bounds read; its content depends on the compiler and linker, not on the graph. `gv-diff render` does not include this case. It should be reported upstream: `doBorder` should pass a properly terminated style (e.g. `"dashed\0\0"`) or `xdot_style` should not assume arguments follow. **Cases** Not a fuzz case: found while porting the renderer (`docs/porting/render.md`, Known differences). The fuzz generator does not produce HTML-like labels. **Files** `tests/fuzz-open/034-html-cell-dashed-style-overread` Visual diff: {{SITE}}/whats-left/html-cell-dashed-style-overread/

title: fdp overlap=compress with cluster edges: C's layout varies run to run (address-dependent ties); the port gives one of C's outputs
body:
fdp with `overlap=compress` and cluster edges: C's layout varies from run to run on the same machine, because a tie inside the overlap removal is broken by heap addresses. The port always draws one of C's layouts.

**Reproducer**

```dot
graph {
  subgraph cluster_a { a1 -- a2 }
  subgraph cluster_b { b1 -- b2 }
  cluster_a -- cluster_b
}
```

```sh
GVBINDIR=<pango-free plugins> dot -Kfdp -Gnormalize=30 -Gsep=+10 -Goverlap=compress -Tsvg repro.gv
graphviz-pure -Kfdp -Gnormalize=30 -Gsep=+10 -Goverlap=compress -Tsvg repro.gv
```

**C output vs port**

```diff
--- c
+++ rust
-node a2 1.1352 0.73586 0.75 0.5 a2 solid ellipse black lightgrey
-node b1 1.7843 1.1106 0.75 0.5 b1 solid ellipse black lightgrey
-node b2 1.1352 0.73586 0.75 0.5 b2 solid ellipse black lightgrey
+node a2 1.1355 0.73604 0.75 0.5 a2 solid ellipse black lightgrey
+node b1 1.1355 0.73604 0.75 0.5 b1 solid ellipse black lightgrey
+node b2 1.7849 1.111 0.75 0.5 b2 solid ellipse black lightgrey
```

C puts `a2` and `b2` at the same place, the port puts `a2` and `b1` there: the pair inside
one cluster comes out mirrored.

On macOS, with the port's math, C gives two arrangements over 10 runs (6x and 4x): the pair inside one cluster comes out mirrored. The port's output is always one of C's.

`tests/fdp/wild_gv16_graphs_fdp_8f3263.gv` (also `tests/wild/gv16_graphs_fdp_8f3263.gv`) with the same flags gives three distinct C outputs over 20 runs (18/1/1) on macOS, and two over 20 runs without `-Gnormalize`.

On the Linux C build the output is stable over 20 runs, but it changes with the allocator: `GLIBC_TUNABLES=glibc.malloc.tcache_count=100` and `MALLOC_MMAP_THRESHOLD_=0` each give a different drawing from the same binary and the same input. The result depends on heap addresses, not on the input.

**Root cause**

The likely source is a heap-address tie inside `removeOverlapAs(compress)` (`lib/neatogen/adjust.c` and the constraint code), the same class as "Ties by address" in `docs/porting/neato.md` (#225) and as the derived-graph ordering of #34: C's result depends on its allocator, so there is no single C answer to match. The exact C line was not confirmed. The port's drawing is one of C's.

**Class**

C nondeterminism or undefined behaviour: the output depends on heap addresses.

**Cases**

`tests/fdp/wild_gv16_graphs_fdp_8f3263.gv`, with the flags above.

title: dot pack: a node of two non-nested clusters is laid out in two components that share its C node and edge records; the port gives each component fresh records
body:
dot's `pack` with a node in two non-nested clusters: C lays the components out on one shared set of node and edge records, so the second component starts from what the first left in them. The port gives every component fresh records, so the two components do not see each other.

**Reproducer**

```dot
digraph "G" {
  pack="true";
  subgraph "cluster_0" {
    "v0" [];
    "v6" [];
  }
  subgraph "cluster_2" {
    "v6" -> "v0";
  }
}
```

```sh
GVBINDIR=<pango-free plugins> dot -Kdot -Tsvg repro.gv
graphviz-pure -Kdot -Tsvg repro.gv
```

**C output vs port**

```diff
--- c
+++ rust
-graph 0 1 2
-node v0 0 0 0.5 0.5 v0 solid ellipse black lightgrey
-node v6 0 0 0.5 0.5 v6 solid ellipse black lightgrey
-edge v6 v0 2 0 0 0 0 0 0 0 0 solid black
-edge v6 v0 2 0 0 0 0 0 0 0 0 solid black
+graph 0 2 2
+node v0 0 0 0.5 0.5 v0 solid ellipse black lightgrey
+node v6 0 1 0.5 0.5 v6 solid ellipse black lightgrey
+edge v6 v0 2 0 0.25 0 1 0.25 0 0 solid black
```

C lays the two components out on the same rank and leaves two edges behind, one from each
component's layout; the port gives every component its own records, so the edge has one
bezier and the two nodes are on different ranks.

C also prints `node "v0" belongs to two non-nested clusters "cluster_2" and "cluster_0"`, and so does the port.

**Root cause**

C's `doDot` (`lib/dotgen/dotinit.c:465-487`) runs `dotLayout` on each `cccomps` component in turn. The components are subgraphs of the root, so a node or edge that belongs to two of them has **one** `Agnodeinfo_t`/`Agedgeinfo_t`. The second layout starts from whatever the first left in those records, and `new_spline` (`lib/common/splines.c:212`) *appends* to `ED_spl`, so a shared edge ends up with one bezier from each layout. The port builds each component with fresh records (`Dot::new_component`, `crates/graphviz-pure-layout/src/dotgen/pack.rs:433`) and copies them back with "last one wins".

**Why the port should not match**

This is C's error path: C reports the node as belonging to two non-nested clusters and then lays out on shared records. Matching it would mean reproducing what `dot_init_node` and `dot_init_edge` do not reset, on an input C reports as an error. `docs/porting/crashes.md` records it as not matched (#101, and #352, the same case).

**Class**

C's error path.

**Cases**

Fuzz seed 1548 (`python3 -I scripts/fuzz-gen.py --seed 1548`), minimised with the bounding-box fix from #100 applied.
